chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hammad, from Al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
There was a slave girl for Ali ibn Al-Husayn (peace be upon him) who used to slaughter for him whenever he so intended.
ai.seo_question: Is it permissible for a slave girl to slaughter an animal for her master's consumption?
ai.summary: This narration from al-Kafi highlights the juristic principle that the validity of slaughter depends on the master's intention (niyyah) rather than the physical act of the agent, thereby validating the slaughter performed by a slave girl on behalf of Ali ibn al-Husayn (Zayn al-Abidin). It serves as a foundational evidence in Shia fiqh for the permissibility of using non-independent agents, such as children or the blind, provided the ownership and intent remain with the master.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from hammad, from Al Halby, 
Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> has said:
‘There used to be a slave girl for Ali<sup>asws</sup> Bin Al-Husayn<sup>asws</sup> who used to slaughter for him<sup>asws</sup> whenever he<sup>asws</sup> so intended’.
en.sarwar: 7. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ibn abu ‘ Umayr from Hammad from al-Halabiy who has said the following: “Abu ‘ Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said that
Ali ibn al-Husayn, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, had a slave-girl who would slaughter animals if he (the Imam) wanted.”’
